questions.question: What is an element of $A\times B$?
options: A subset containing all elements of $A$ and $B$
An ordered pair $(a,b)$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$
An unordered pair whose entries may come from either set
A number obtained by multiplying elements of $A$ and $B$
questions.explanation: An element of $A\times B$ is an ordered pair $(a,b)$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$.
questions.source_support: Definition: A x B = {(a,b): a in A, b in B}.
questions.skill_detail: Recall the definition of Cartesian product.
option_explanations: It is a pair, not a subset of $A\cup B$.
The pair is ORDERED, not unordered.
It is a pair, not a product of numbers.

questions.question: What does $A\times B$ list?
options: Only elements that lie in both $A$ and $B$ (the intersection)
Every possible pairing of one element of $A$ with one element of $B$
questions.explanation: By definition $A\times B=\{(a,b):a\in A,\ b\in B\}$, so each element of $A$ is paired with each element of $B$, producing all ordered pairs.
questions.source_support: Interpretation: a Cartesian product lists every possible pairing of an element of A with an element of B.

questions.question: For finite sets, how is $\operatorname{card}(A\times B)$ computed?
questions.explanation: For finite sets, $\operatorname{card}(A\times B)=\operatorname{card}(A)\cdot\operatorname{card}(B)$.
questions.source_support: Relevant result: card(A x B)=card(A)card(B) for finite A and B.
